claims.proposition_evaluated: The $100 million approved for bike lanes (capital profile CM-20-0330, 2023-2026 capital budget, December 2022) is almost double the City's annual snow-clearing budget (the 2022 Snow and Ice Control 'Expenditure & Transfers' cell in the Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget).
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict figure. Numerator: CM-20-0330 approved at $100,000 thousand (Appendix A printed page 103, in $000s; profile sheet pages 540-543; Council Capital Budget Amendment 7, carried 9 to 4, minutes of City Council - Budget November 30 to December 16, 2022, where the profile is named 'Bike Plan Implementation - Approach 3'). Per-year approved: 5,950 (2023), 26,750 (2024), 33,650 (2025), 33,650 (2026); approved average $25.0 million a year. One later amendment: Spring 2025 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment (FCS02852, City Council June 10, 2025) moved $430 thousand to profile 25-25-9506 Dunluce Neighbourhood and Alley Renewal, leaving 99,570. Primary denominator: Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, Parks & Roads Services, Program Summary, Snow and Ice Control, row 'Expenditure & Transfers', column '2022 Budget', printed page 212 (PDF 216), 64,466 in $000s. Ratio 100,000 / 64,466 = 1.551. Primary cutoffs: Partially supported (1.5 to below 1.8). Alternative cutoffs: Partially supported (1.25 to below 1.7). Alternative A, budget as amended in-year: I found three council additions to the 2022 Snow and Ice Control budget in force on 2022-12-12, each one-time: (1) March 14, 2022, $2.3 million of 2021 program surplus applied to 2022 costs; (2) April 19, 2022, Spring 2022 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment, FCS01143 Attachment 1, 'Enhanced Snow Clearing Pilot costs', expense 14,300 funded from the Financial Stabilization Reserve, carried 13 to 0; (3) July 4, 2022, item 6.6 CO01277, $4.7 million from the Financial Stabilization Reserve for the 2022 portion of the 2022-2023 winter, carried 13 to 0. Amended budget 64,466 + 2,300 + 14,300 + 4,700 = 85,766; ratio 1.166; Contradicted under both cutoff sets. Without the March carry-forward, 83,466 and 1.198, still Contradicted under both. The other reviewers' July-only reading gives 69,166 and 1.446, Contradicted under primary cutoffs and Partially supported under alternative cutoffs. The City's own year-end 2022 Snow and Ice Control expense budget (Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2022, FCS01656 Attachment 1) is 79,474, giving 1.258, Contradicted under primary cutoffs and just Partially supported under alternative cutoffs; the year-end figure is lower than my summed amendments, so a reconciliation the City has not published (offsets or reallocations) sits between them. Alternative B, 2023 approved: the brief's named cell does not exist. The 2023-2026 Operating Budget and Plans (804 PDF pages, re-checked on 2026-09-02) has no Snow and Ice Control program summary table; the program appears on 14 pages as a service description, in the Enhanced Snow and Ice Control Service Standards package (page 105: 4,043 / 3,725 / 2,477 / 721 for 2023-2026 in $000s plus 275 in Community Standards and Neighbourhoods) and in the Parks and Roads Services branch section, which reports branch totals only. Operating Budget Amendment 18 (moved A. Sohi, carried 12 to 1, M. Janz opposed) funded that package at 20 per cent ongoing: 2023 $3,768,000 Parks and Roads plus $274,600 Community Standards. The nearest City figure for the 2023 program after the amendment is $60.9 million (City Budget Engagement Fact Sheet, undated as to year; Global News 2022-12-20 states it as the 2023 total; CBC 2022-12-16 reports a $56.9 million base plus the $4 million amendment, which sum to it). Ratio 100 / 60.9 = 1.642, Partially supported under both cutoff sets. Using the year-end 2023 adjusted expense budget of 63,574 (FCS02229 Attachment 1) instead: 1.573, Partially supported under both. Context, not denominators: 2022 'Total Net Operating Requirement' 63,653 ($000s; the branch summary on printed page 205 shows 63,666), ratio 1.571; 2022 actual gross expenditure 97,571 (FCS01656 Attachment 1; heavier snowfall and freezing rain, $13.0 million January to April and $5.0 million October to December over budget), ratio 1.025. Qualification 1, like-for-like: (a) 2023 approved CM-20-0330 5,950 against 2023 snow 60,900 = 0.098 (against 63,574: 0.094); the bike-lane allocation for 2023 was about one tenth of the year's snow budget. (b) $100 million against four years of approved snow budget: 60,900 (2023) + 67,090 (2024, year-end adjusted expense budget, FCS02841 Attachment 1) + 68,618 (2025 Approved Budget, FCS03370 Attachment 1 page 6) + 72,645 (2026 Approved Budget, same page) = 269,253; ratio 0.371. The four figures are not on one basis (see limitations). Qualification 2, actuals: CM-20-0330 by year by differencing cumulative to-date actuals: 2023 807 (FCS02228 Att. 2, Dec 31, 2023); 2024 10,496 - 807 = 9,689 (FCS02842 Att. 2); 2025 39,984 - 10,496 = 29,488 (FCS03313 Att. 2, Dec 31, 2025); total spent to December 31, 2025: 39,984, 40.2 per cent of the current 99,570 budget; actual average $13.3 million a year over three completed years against an approved average of $25.0 million. Snow and Ice Control actuals, program-summary basis (FCS03370): 51,750 / 64,749 / 66,588; ratios 0.016 (2023), 0.150 (2024), 0.443 (2025); three-year 39,984 / 183,087 = 0.218. On the Operating Financial Update basis (54,917 / 72,086 / 76,648): 0.015, 0.134, 0.385; three-year 0.196. Qualification 3: net figure ratio 1.571 as above. Qualification 4: no constant-dollar restatement applied; all figures nominal. Position after cross-review: unchanged. The other two reviewers reach the same primary ratio from the same cell; I keep Partially supported because 1.551 falls in the brief's band, not because they do. Where we differ is Alternative A, where I hold that the full amendment list makes the as-amended reading Contradicted under both cutoff sets. Definition sensitivity: primary Partially supported; Alternative A Contradicted; Alternative B Partially supported. The finding is definition-sensitive on the in-year amendment question and the story should say so beside the verdict.

limitations: The comparison is not like-for-like: a four-year capital authorization against one year's operating budget. On the holder's own terms the ratio is 1.55; on a like-for-like basis the bike-lane program is about one tenth of the 2023 snow budget (2023 allocations) or about 0.37 of four years of snow budget.

The 2023-2026 Operating Budget prints no Snow and Ice Control program cell, so Alternative B rests on a City fact-sheet figure ($60.9 million) whose year is fixed by media reports and by reconciliation with the amendment, not by the document itself.

The four-year snow sum mixes bases: 2023 from the fact sheet, 2024 from a year-end adjusted budget, 2025 and 2026 from the FCS03370 program summary. A single published series of approved gross program budgets for 2023-2026 does not exist.

Snow and Ice Control actuals exist on two City bases (Operating Financial Update tables versus the FCS03370 Program Summary by Account Category) that differ by $3 million to $10 million a year; the program summary carries almost no labour cost because SNIC labour sits in Mobility Infrastructure Services, whereas the 2022 primary cell carried 225.9 FTE. Cross-year and budget-to-actual comparisons therefore carry a basis caveat.

Alternative A depends on how many 2022 amendments count. The City's year-end 2022 expense budget (79,474) is below the primary cell plus the three amendments I found (85,766), so some offsetting adjustment is unpublished; either figure is Contradicted under the primary cutoffs.
No constant-dollar restatement applied; all figures nominal Canadian dollars.
unknowns: The full 2022 ledger reconciling 64,466 plus the three identified amendments (85,766) to the year-end expense budget of 79,474.
Whether the fact sheet's $60.9 million is a gross or a net program figure.
Which of the two City actuals bases the City would regard as the program's official gross expenditure for 2023-2025.

claims.suggested_one_line: The $100 million bike-lane program is 1.55 times the City's adopted 2022 snow-clearing budget of $64.5 million, well short of double, and the gap widens once 2022's in-year snow top-ups are counted.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Partially supported. The $100 million approved for capital profile CM-20-0330 is 1.55 times the 2022 Snow and Ice Control budget as adopted ($64.5 million). That is half again, not almost double. Council added $21.3 million to the 2022 snow budget during the year, which takes the ratio down to 1.17; against the 2023 snow budget of $60.9 million it is 1.64. The $100 million is spread over four years, and only $40.0 million of it had been spent by the end of 2025.
suggested_tldr: CM-20-0330: $100 million approved for 2023-2026, not per year; $40.0 million spent by December 31, 2025.
Adopted 2022 snow budget: $64.5 million; ratio 1.55, which the brief's cutoffs class as Partially supported.
With 2022's three in-year snow additions ($21.3 million), the ratio falls to 1.17; against the 2023 snow budget ($60.9 million) it is 1.64.
Like-for-like, the 2023 bike-lane allocation ($5.95 million) was about a tenth of the 2023 snow budget.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In the City's 2023-2026 capital budget as adopted in December 2022, roads (the brief's roads-only profile boundary) get $1.8 billion, about eighteen times the $100 million for CM-20-0330.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict figure. Primary boundary sum from Appendix A (in $000s): Roads-labelled profiles 1,116,532 (18 profiles; 21-20-2100 and 14-66-2570 excluded as predeclared); Neighbourhood Renewal 722,289 (11 profiles); three unlabelled vehicle-carrying bridges 106,882 (23-24-0300 High Level 97,000; 21-24-9301 Latta 9,832; 21-24-9302 Glenora 50). Total 1,945,703; ratio 19.46. Supported under primary cutoffs (at least $1.5 billion) and alternative cutoffs (at least $1.62 billion). All three reviewers reach 1,945,703 independently, and gpt's per-profile list with sheet pages matches my reading of the 161 sheets; no sheet label differs from the editor's membership. Required alternative: Table 8 'Adopted Capital Budget by Service' (printed page 56, $ millions), under 'Movement of People and Goods', 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' Growth 622.8, Renewal 1,171.2, 2023-2026 total 1,794.0 (2027 and beyond 108.6; all years 1,902.6). Ratio 17.94; Supported under both cutoff sets. It contains CM-20-0330 and other active-pathway funding and is not a roads total; the councillor's $1.8 billion matches this combined line, not any roads-only figure the City prints. Widest reading: primary plus the six streetscape and pedestrian-realm profiles, 80,145 (gpt's list, arithmetic checked), 2,025,848, ratio 20.26, Supported under both. Narrowest: Roads-labelled only, 1,116,532, ratio 11.17, Partially supported under both cutoff sets. Sensitivity I flagged in round 1 and keep: the four Yellowhead Trail profiles (493,400, including CM-99-9600 Project Delivery 376,255) carry the 'Roads' label on their sheets but Table 8 presents them as the transformational 'Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion' outside the Active Pathways and Roads Service; without them the primary sum is 1,452,303, ratio 14.52, Partially supported under both cutoff sets. gpt adds that Traffic Safety-presented profiles also carry the Roads label. The brief fixes the boundary by sheet label, so they stay in; the reader should know the primary result depends on them. Definition sensitivity: primary Supported, required alternative Supported; the verdict is not definition-sensitive on the brief's test, though the narrowest reading and the Yellowhead sensitivity both give Partially supported. Qualification 2, as amended: no roads-only as-amended total is published and I did not rebuild it profile by profile. Whole-budget trajectory: Fall 2024 SCBA (FCS02530rev Attachment 1, City Council December 2, 2024) shows the approved 2023-2026 tax-supported capital budget including 2022 carry-forward at $9,073 million and the total capital budget after that adjustment at $10,970 million (all years), with a recommended net increase of $151.8 million; Fall 2025 SCBA (FCS03159 Attachment 1, November 24, 2025) shows $11,612 million after adjustment, net increase $98.2 million; the City's Budget and Finances page states that on June 16, 2026 council approved the final adjustment of the cycle, a $126.6 million (1.10 per cent) net increase to an $11.56 billion capital budget. CM-20-0330 was reduced by $430 thousand on June 10, 2025 (Spring 2025 SCBA). Qualification 3, actuals: no consistent published series for the whole roads set. The Capital Financial Update at December 31, 2025 gives to-date actuals for the largest roads profiles: Terwillegar Drive 19-22-9006 209,132 of 327,220 current approved; High Level Bridge 23-24-0300 4,635 of 200,000; CM-24-0000 26,360 of 56,078; CM-22-0000 16,841 of 29,492; CM-25-0000 28,029 of 48,522; CM-66-2585 17,897 of 26,569. CM-20-0330 actuals by year: 807 (2023), 9,689 (2024), 29,488 (2025), 39,984 to date of 99,570. Qualification 4, shares on adopted figures: CM-20-0330 is 1.39 per cent of the 2023-2026 adopted capital budget (7,192.5), 1.26 per cent of the all-years total (7,908.2), 1.95 per cent of the transportation portion (Table 8: Movement of People and Goods 2,256.0 + LRT Expansion 2,374.9 + Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion 493.4 = 5,124.3), consistent with the City's own 'about 2 per cent of approximately $5 billion in transportation projects', and 5.57 per cent of the Active Pathways and Roads Service line. The '180'. Global News (2022-12-12) prints 'Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.' $1.8 billion is 18 times $100 million. No other record of the statement was located by any reviewer; the council budget minutes record motions and votes, not floor speech, and no video timestamp was found. The councillor's own page (michaeljanz.ca/bikeplan) says the $100 million 'represents half a percent of the $1.8 Billion dollar capital budget over the same period'; it is 5.6 per cent. Both arithmetic errors belong to the quotation and the holder, not to the budget. Position after cross-review: unchanged, Supported, High. The three reviews agree because the same sheets yield the same sums; my reservation remains that the City itself prints no roads-only total and the primary sum is a construction from labels, which the story should say.

limitations: The City publishes no roads-only capital total. The primary figure is a reproducible construction from sheet labels under the brief's predeclared boundary, and it crosses the City's own service presentation by including Yellowhead Trail and Traffic Safety-presented profiles that carry the 'Roads' label.
Mixed profiles (Neighbourhood Renewal includes sidewalks, alleys and streetlights) are included in full because the City publishes no roadway share.

The $1,794.0 million Table 8 line is the figure the councillor's $1.8 billion matches, and it includes active pathways including CM-20-0330; it must be reported under its full name and never as a roads total.
The as-amended roads-only total to the as-of date was not rebuilt profile by profile; only whole-budget trajectories are reported.
No consistent published series of annual actuals exists for the whole roads profile set; only to-date actuals for the largest profiles are reported.
The widest-reading total relies on gpt's per-profile amounts for the six added profiles; I checked the arithmetic, not each sheet.
All figures nominal Canadian dollars; no constant-dollar restatement.
unknowns: Whether the councillor said '18' or '180' on the floor; no council video timestamp or transcript was located by any reviewer, and the minutes do not record floor speech.
The roadway-only share of the Neighbourhood Renewal and other mixed profiles.
The as-amended total for the primary profile set after all supplemental capital budget adjustments through 2026-09-02.

claims.suggested_one_line: On the City's own profile labels, roads and neighbourhood renewal get $1.95 billion in the 2023-2026 capital budget, about 19 times the $100 million for bike lanes; the councillor's $1.8 billion matches the City's combined 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' line, which includes the bike lanes.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported. Summing every 2023-2026 capital profile the City labels 'Roads' or 'Neighbourhood Renewal', plus three vehicle bridges, gives $1.95 billion, 19.5 times the $100 million bike-lane profile. The $1.8 billion the councillor cited is the City's 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' line ($1.794 billion), which includes bike lanes and pathways. Read narrowly, 'Roads'-labelled profiles alone total $1.12 billion, still eleven times the bike-lane figure. The quotation's '180 times' is an arithmetic slip; $1.8 billion is 18 times $100 million.
suggested_tldr: Roads-only profiles under the brief's boundary: $1,945.7 million, 19.5 times $100 million.
City's combined 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' line: $1,794.0 million, 17.9 times; it includes the bike lanes and is not a roads total.
Bike-lane profile is 1.4 per cent of the 2023-2026 capital budget and about 2 per cent of transportation capital; '180 times' should have been 18.
